name: Hair fibres (Toppik)

card.summary: Keratin-style cosmetic fibres that cling to existing hair to disguise thinning; a cover-up rather than a treatment, with a rare eye-injury case report.
card.aka: Toppik, hair building fibers, reconstructive hair fibers
card.note: A case report describes a fibre entering the eye and causing uveitis.

quick.overview:
Hair fibres such as Toppik are fine powders that bind to existing hair by static electricity to make thinning areas look fuller. They disguise hair loss rather than treating it.

Published research is limited to a 2017 microscopy analysis of five brands and a 2020 case report of eye injury.
quick.mechanism: Electrostatically charged fibres adhere to the hair shaft, thickening its appearance and reducing visible scalp. Effects last until washed out.
quick.risks: A 2020 case report described anterior uveitis after a fibre from a hair-building product entered the eye of a 73-year-old man.

lead: Hair fibres, sold under brands such as Toppik, are cosmetic powders made of tiny fibres that cling to existing hair and make thinning areas look fuller. They are used by men and women to disguise hair loss at the crown, part line or temples, giving the look of denser hair within minutes and without surgery or medication [1].

A 2017 study in the International Journal of Trichology describes these products as reconstructive hair fibres, an electrostatic adherent powder that bonds to the hair shaft and can disguise hair loss, and used scanning electron microscopy and X-ray microanalysis to compare the shape, structure and chemical composition of five brands [1].

Hair fibres sit among the concealment options for hair loss, alongside comb-overs, hats, wigs and toupees, while medications and transplants are separate treatment routes [2]. They change how hair looks rather than how it grows.

chain: Fibres are applied to thinning hair
Electrostatic attraction binds them to existing strands
Scalp shows less through the hair and density looks higher
angle.text: Fibres thicken the apparent diameter of existing hair, so thin patches show less scalp. The effect is temporary and visible immediately, which is why users apply them before events or daily as part of styling.

paras: Reconstructive hair fibres are described as organic fibres of fine powder that carry an electrostatic charge so they adhere to the existing hair shaft. Lab analysis of five brands examined their shape, morphology and chemical composition [1]. The fibres do not grow hair or affect the follicle.

Wikipedia's hair loss article lists concealment strategies including comb-overs, hats and wigs or toupees, which range widely in quality and cost [2]. Hair fibres are a topical option within this group, while minoxidil, finasteride, dutasteride and hair transplantation address loss itself [2].
No studies found of clinical outcomes. A laboratory study analysed the shape, structure and chemical composition of five brands of reconstructive hair fibres [1].

The reported harm is a single case report from 2020 of a 73-year-old man with his first episode of acute anterior uveitis, in whom a white fibre was found penetrating the cornea into the anterior chamber; he identified it as coming from a cosmetic hair-building product. The authors discussed earlier literature on small foreign fibres causing eye disease [3].

timeline.event: A laboratory study compares five brands of reconstructive hair fibres by electron microscopy [1].
A case report describes uveitis linked to a fibre from a hair enhancement product [3].
